cam-cast-subtype.basis: sand: carbon steel — sand casting has the lowest tooling NRE and no upper size limit; ductile-iron/steel castings finish by fettling + machining

cam-cast-yield.basis: sand carbon-steel yield band 0.45–0.6, midpoint (feeding scales with the alloy's shrinkage; engineering-typical band, not sourced — the foundry's method yield replaces it)

cam-sand-core.basis: no undercut along the best pull — the pattern draws cleanly, no core; per-part core (sand, binder, labour), material consumable — a default band (UK, engineering-typical, not sourced), not a core-shop quote

cam-hpdc-die-cost.basis: sand toolmaker shop model: 215 toolroom hours + aluminium plate + bought-outs from a 105 cm² parting footprint × 12 impressions on the plate, 0 core box(es) (0 undercut face(s)) — a quotation overrides this

cam-hpdc-die-life.basis: aluminium match-plate life 100,000 moulds × 12 impression(s) a mould on the automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) = 1,200,000 castings — the pattern priced is an aluminium plate, so its life is an aluminium match plate: published 10,000–50,000 moulds (Supro MFG), 25k–100k to first refurbishment and 80k–150k total (YB Metal), 100k–500k for a metal pattern (Bowmanville) — supplier pages that disagree ×10; 100,000 total is CostVision engineering judgement, and the refurbishments between are not costed. A steel plate lasts up to 500,000 moulds (DISA, said of an aluminium-casting foundry) but none is priced; a foundry's pattern life replaces this

cam-sand-ct.basis: automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class): 12 impression(s) of 132 × 120 mm (+50 mm gating) on a 950 × 700 mm mould (impressions = the smallest of: free fit 20 (the footprint + 50 mm a side for gating, engineering-typical, not sourced); 60 % plate rule (DISA Application Manual §2.1.4: "Plate area covered by the pattern and the gating system should not exceed 60% of the total plate area" (the maker's manual, read from a third-party upload)): each impression is the footprint + 50 mm a side, 182.00 × 170.00 mm = 30,940 mm², and 0.6 × 950 × 700 mm² ÷ 30,940 mm² = 12.90 → 12 (rounded down) (the sand : iron ≥ 5 : 1 limit is stated for iron foundries — not applied to this metal) → 12 — the 60 % plate rule binds), 280 uncored moulds/h (DISA 270-280, 950 × 700 mm mould (the smallest 270 size), 280 uncored / 250 cored moulds/h at 200 mm mould thickness (DISA General Specifications, 04/23) — the rated maximum; the 270 mould thickness is not in the specification read, so a casting's depth is not checked against it) — 1 ÷ 280 ÷ 12 = 0.000298 h, the line's time per casting, not the cooling time. Line: 50,000 castings a year = 5,000 moulds a year on the semi-automatic flask line (HWS HSP-2D class) (10 a mould) ≥ 5,000 → the automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) (the line threshold is CostVision engineering judgement, not sourced — no published source gives one; 5,000 follows AFS: metal pattern equipment over ~5,000 castings a year); loading 4,167 moulds ÷ 280 moulds/h = 15 h of the line's 4,800 h a year (book hours × utilisation) = 0.3 %

cam-sand-line.basis: automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class): 50,000 castings a year = 5,000 moulds a year on the semi-automatic flask line (HWS HSP-2D class) (10 a mould) ≥ 5,000 → the automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) (the line threshold is CostVision engineering judgement, not sourced — no published source gives one; 5,000 follows AFS: metal pattern equipment over ~5,000 castings a year); loading 4,167 moulds ÷ 280 moulds/h = 15 h of the line's 4,800 h a year (book hours × utilisation) = 0.3 %

cam-cast-lab.basis: foundry operative on the moulding / die-casting line and at the fettling bench

cam-fettle-min.basis: none at the bench — a 2.5 kg carbon steel casting off the automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) is fettled on a robotic grinding cell (see the robotic fettling cell)

cam-fettle-cell-sec.basis: a 2.5 kg carbon steel casting off the automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) is fettled on a robotic grinding cell: robotic grinding cell 40 s a casting, one operator to two cells (Malleable Castings time study, high-volume ductile iron 0.1–30 kg: manual 45 s, cell 40 s; published range to 260 s on a 22 kg heavy-flash casting)

cam-ht-cost.basis: cast steel is normalised to refine the as-cast grain — £0.35/kg × the as-cast kg (the advisor's stress-relieve / normalise rate, UK; engineering-typical, not sourced — a heat treater's quote replaces it)

cam-ht-route.basis: carbon steel — the aluminium heat-treat station does not apply (see the heat-treat cost)

cam-shot-blast.basis: sand castings are blasted to remove the moulding sand, scale and fins — 3.04 kg as cast (finished + machining stock) ÷ 600 kg/h (the low end of a 0.5–2 t/h tumble / hanger blast; engineering-typical, not sourced) × (blast machine £25.07/h + operator £24.60/h), min £0.10 = £0.2516 (CostVision engineering heuristic)

cam-cast-manning.basis: automatic vertical flaskless line (DISAMATIC 270 class) crew of 3: 3 operators a DISAMATIC line with manual pouring (Trakya Döküm: 3 → 2 with automatic pouring, DISA, c. 2025) — the line's capital excludes an automatic pourer, so the manual-pouring crew is taken

cam-new-sand.basis: new silica sand added at 15 % of the poured weight (the midpoint of 10–20 %) and the same tonnage discarded, in 2014 prices not escalated: new sand €45/t + disposal €43/t = €88/t; €88 ÷ €1.1965/£ = £73.5478/t of sand; 0.15 × £73.5478 = £11.0322/t poured (UK) — EU JRC SF BREF 2024 §3.2.1.4.4 (new sand 10–20 % of poured metal) and Tables 3.21–3.22 (DE UBA 2014: new sand €45/t, disposal €43/t), grade B. It replaces the engineering-typical £0.01/kg poured "green-sand additions"; bentonite and coal dust are NOT costed (bentonite €228/t is published, no consumption a tonne poured)

cam-ladle-kwh.basis: ladle preheat 200 kWh per tonne of liquid metal poured — the midpoint of 100–300 kWh/t for steel foundries (EU JRC SF BREF 2024, BAT-AEPL Tables 4.1 (iron) and 4.2 (steel), kWh per tonne of liquid metal, grade B); natural-gas burner assumed (CostVision engineering judgement, not sourced), so the kWh are costed as gas at the costed country's tariff

cam-dust-kwh.basis: dust extraction / off-gas cleaning 20 kWh of electricity per tonne of good casting (German data restated in the EU JRC SF BREF 2024 §2.3.8.1 (flue-gas cleaning ~20 kWh per tonne of good casting), grade B), at the costed country's tariff

cam-plant-kwh.basis: ESTIMATE (grade D — an inference, not a published figure): other plant electricity beyond melting and holding (sand plant, moulding, cleaning, compressed air, services) 0.45–0.5 kWh/kg good casting, midpoint 0.475 (US DOE "Energy Use in Selected Metalcasting Facilities – 2003": a cupola ductile-iron green-sand plant used 720 kWh/t of electricity in all; with its two 1.2 MW channel holding furnaces taken out, ~0.45–0.50 kWh/kg good casting is left (the research's inference, grade D)) − 0.02 kWh/kg dust extraction charged on its own line = 455 kWh per tonne of good casting, at the costed country's tariff. NOT costed (no published price found): furnace and ladle refractory (8–9 kg/t molten on induction, 1994 data — no current price), the metallurgical lab a melt, the pouring and sand-plant crew beyond the moulding-line crew and the melt shop's operator-hours, bentonite and coal-dust additions (bentonite €228/t is published, no consumption a tonne poured), and on steel castings riser cut-off, weld repair and steel refractory wear

cam-sf-route.basis: not asked yet — costed bare (answer "Is the part coated?" to price a finish)

cam-sf-area.basis: measured surface 628.3 cm² = 0.0628 m² — the whole wetted surface; a masked or machined-after-coating face is in it
